summary: Board View: Card size control (Compact / Detailed) as in the design
description:
### What

Bring Board View's density in line with the design:

* A Card size control on Board View with two options, Compact and Detailed. Detailed is the default.
* Detailed shows the full card, as today.
* Compact tightens the card padding and the gap between card lines, and hides: the hours, created date and progress bar line; the technicians and total line; and the waiting-on-parts marker.
* Card size is saved per user, separately from Tech View's density.
* It takes the toolbar spot the Density control left in SV-11580, so Column Selection and Card size sit side by side as in the design.

Before building, confirm the exact sizes and what Compact hides against the live design file.

### Why

Follow-up to SV-11580, which hides Board View's Density for Thursday's release because it barely changes anything.

### How to check

* Board View shows Card size with Compact and Detailed; a new user starts on Detailed.
* Compact matches the design card for card: tighter spacing, and the three lines above hidden.
* The choice survives a reload, logout and login, and switching to Tech View and back.
* Tech View's density is unaffected.

### Design and PRD

[Work Orders design file (Branko)](https://claude.ai/design/p/787fef1a-9523-43cc-bd06-f88765051d21?file=Work+Orders.dc.html), Board View. [Board & Tech View PRD v71](https://shopview.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/~7120207b6068952672480db1a06bd810e23ba1/pages/845185030), Story 6.

summary: Tech View / Board View – Padlock Shows No Tooltip on Hover, Only the Browser's Plain Hint
description:
## Description

**What the PRD requires:** the padlock after an Invoiced or Paid work order's number has a **tooltip** carrying the locked words (PRD **S4-N6**: "The same words are the tooltip on the card’s or row’s lock icon"). The design draws its tooltips as a dark box with light text, opening above what is hovered — the same style the app already uses for the display switcher.

**What happens instead:** resting the mouse on the padlock opens no tooltip. Only the browser's own plain hint appears after a delay, in the browser's style, not the app's.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Sign in, open **Work Orders**, click the **All** tab and click **Tech View**.
2. Find a row whose work order is **Invoiced** (a small padlock sits right after the number).
3. Rest the mouse on the padlock.

    * No dark tooltip opens above the padlock.
    * As a check, rest the mouse on **Board View** in the display switcher: a dark tooltip with light text opens.
    

**Actual Result:**

* No tooltip opens on the padlock; only the browser's plain hint appears.

**Expected Result:**

* A tooltip opens above the padlock, in the app's dark tooltip style, with the locked words.

summary: Technician filter: list the "Deleted technician" column
description:
### What

The Technician filter in Board View and Tech View lists everyone who gets a group or column, except the "Deleted technician" column (work orders whose lead technician was deleted in Settings, S3-R20e). Add it.

* List "Deleted technician" last, after the deactivated technicians, with the same grey Inactive label as its column.
* It is listed only while that column exists (at least one work order whose lead technician was deleted).
* Choosing it shows only the Deleted technician column or group; it combines with the other filters like any other choice.

### Why

Your rule is that the filter lists everyone who has a column, so the filter and the board agree. It is also the quickest way to find work that needs a new lead.

### How to check

* Staging Heavy Duty - 9919, Board View: type "Deleted" in the Technician list; "Deleted technician" shows, last, with the Inactive label.
* Tick it: only the Deleted technician column shows (5 work orders today). Same in Tech View.
* At a location with no such work orders, it is not listed.

### PRD

[Board & Tech View PRD v73](https://shopview.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/~7120207b6068952672480db1a06bd810e23ba1/pages/845185030), S1-R15. Raised by Bilal on SV-11575, 2026-10-21.

summary: Undo a lead technician change in Board View and Tech View
description:
### What

Add Undo to the lead technician change message in Board View and Tech View, as the Board & Tech View PRD v78 describes (S4-R32, timing in S4-R16).

* After a lead change, the message shows an Undo button and stays 5 seconds, held open while hovered.
* Undo puts the work order back exactly as it was: the previous lead technician (or Unassigned), its previous place in that technician's order, and any shifts the change cleared. Removed shifts come back as they were; a shift ended at the moment of the change gets its original end time back. Each labor line goes back to the technician it had before the change, and a line that had none goes back to none (Undo does not apply the normal lead-change line rules).
* Undo is itself a lead change: it records its own audit entry, follows the Invoiced or Paid rule (an invoiced or paid work order can't be moved back), and shows no shift-clearing prompt.
* After Undo, the message reads "Assignment undone", with no Undo button on it.
* If Undo can't be saved, nothing changes and the alert "Couldn’t undo the change. Move the work order back by hand." shows.

### Why

Split out of SV-11522 and SV-11524 so those can close on Thursday's work. Undo is the biggest piece, because it rebuilds cleared shifts. Until it ships, the lead change message has no Undo and closes after 2.6 seconds.

### How to check

* TestRail C682426: Undo puts the work order back with its old lead and in its old place.
* TestRail C682427: Undo brings back the shifts that a lead change cleared.
* TestRail C682428: Undo cannot move back a work order that was invoiced in the meantime.
* Check it in both Board View and Tech View.

### PRD

[Board & Tech View PRD v78](https://shopview.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/~7120207b6068952672480db1a06bd810e23ba1/pages/845185030/Work+Orders+Board+View+Tech+View+Display+Options), S4-R16 and S4-R32.

summary: Board View and Tech View – Empty Locations Show No "Add Technician" Button and No "Nothing Here Yet" State
description:
## Description

**When a location has no technicians, the Work Orders board should help the user add them: an "Add Technician" button under "No technicians yet", and — when the location also has no work orders — a "Nothing here yet" state with both Create Work Order and Add Technician.** On staging neither is there.

For example,

* at a location with work orders but no technicians, Board View and Tech View show "No technicians yet" and its text, but no "Add Technician" button
* at a location with no technicians and no work orders, both views read "No work orders yet" and "Create a work order and assign a technician to see it here." with only a Create Work Order button
* "Nothing here yet" and "Add technicians and create your first work order to track work by tech." never appear

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Sign in to staging as an Admin.
2. Make a location with no technicians and two **Approved** work orders (for example **ZZAUTOTEST F2 No Tech Shop**), and a second location with no technicians and no work orders (for example **ZZAUTOTEST Location Empty**).
3. Change location to the first one. Open **Work Orders**, click the **All** tab and click **Tech View**, then **Board View**.

    * Both show only **Unassigned**, then "No technicians yet" and "Add technicians to assign work orders. Until then, every work order stays in Unassigned."
    * There is no **Add Technician** button.
    
4. Change location to the second one. Open **Work Orders** > **All** and click **Board View**, then **Tech View**.

    * Both read "No work orders yet" and "Create a work order and assign a technician to see it here." with only **Create Work Order**.
    

**Actual Result:**

* No **Add Technician** button anywhere, and the "Nothing here yet" state never shows.

**Expected Result:**

* The PRD says: **"When the location has no technicians but has work orders, Tech View and Board View show only Unassigned, followed by the design’s state: the user-round icon, “No technicians yet”, then “Add technicians to assign work orders. Until then, every work order stays in Unassigned.”, with an Add Technician button. When the location has neither technicians nor work orders, the state reads “Nothing here yet”, then “Add technicians and create your first work order to track work by tech.”, with the Create Work Order button of S1-N1c and the Add Technician button."**

summary: Board View / Tech View – a lead change made just before a filter or search change can leave the board stale
description:
**What:** A drag or a Reassign remembers which board it started on before its request goes out. If a filter, search or location change switches the board while the request is out, the answer is written into the old board only, so the new board keeps showing the old lead until the next refresh.

**Also:** a board read that starts while the change (or its Undo) is in flight and lands after its answer can still show the board from before the change, until the next read.

**Where:** `useLeadBoardMove.ts` (\~221, \~299), `useLeadBoardReassign.ts` (\~115, \~172). Already on main; not caused by SV-11567.

**Fix idea:** in `useLeadBoard.commit()`, a board change made while a move is in flight owes a read of the new board. SV-11567's Undo already does this (PR #3982, SR-1).

**How to check:** Board View with a slow network: drag a card to another technician and type in Search straight away. Clear the search: the card shows under the right technician without a manual refresh.

Found in the #3982 self-review.

summary: Work Orders Analytics – Search Text Is Sent to Google Analytics, Although the PRD Forbids It
description:
## Description

**What the PRD requires:** the usage records that Work Orders sends to Google Analytics may hold only field names and setting values — never search text, names, numbers or amounts (PRD **S12-R5**: "Analytics may contain predefined field keys and setting values, but no displayed record values, names, identifiers, search text, or dollar amounts.").

**What happens instead:** every Work Orders usage record also carries the address of the page. After someone types in the Work Orders **Search** box, that address contains what they typed (for example a customer name), so the search text is sent to Google Analytics with every record.

**Why it happens:**

* the Work Orders page keeps the search in its address (`/workorders?search=...`)
* Google Analytics sends the page address (`page_location`) with every event by default, so each Work Orders record (display shown, fields loaded, density loaded) carries it
* the records' own settings are clean — only the page address leaks the search text

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Sign in to production and open **Work Orders** from the top menu.
2. Open the browser's developer tools (F12) and click the **Network** tab; type `collect` in its filter box.
3. In the Work Orders **Search** box, type a customer name, for example `ZZAUTOTEST Bravo GA`.

    * The page address changes to `.../workorders?search=ZZAUTOTEST+Bravo+GA`.
    
4. Click **Tech View** in the display switcher.

    * New **collect** requests to Google Analytics appear in the Network tab.
    
5. Click one of them and look at its **dl** (page location) value.

    * It reads `https://app.shopview.com/workorders?search=ZZAUTOTEST Bravo GA` — the search text.
    

**Actual Result:**

* Each Work Orders usage record sent to Google Analytics carries the search text inside the page address.

**Expected Result:**

* As the PRD requires (S12-R5), no usage record contains search text (nor names, numbers or amounts); the page address sent with Work Orders records leaves the search out.

## Screenshots

![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=229aa3b0-c1ec-4c15-aee1-bfdc09f7327e&&collection=&height=757&occurrenceKey=null&width=2000&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null)

summary: Board View and Tech View – Locked Work Orders Still Show the Old "Can't Be Changed" Sentence
description:
## Description

**On an Invoiced or Paid work order, the short words "Invoiced · can't be reassigned" (or "Paid · can't be reassigned") should show wherever the lead technician can't be changed.** On staging the old long sentence still shows instead.

For example,

* the lock icon next to the work order number shows the hover text `The lead technician can't be changed once a work order is Invoiced or Paid.`
* the greyed-out **Reassign lead technician** and **Unassign** items in **More actions** show the tooltip `The lead technician can't be changed once a work order is Invoiced or Paid.`
* while the work order is dragged over another technician's column (Board View) or group (Tech View), the note at the top shows the same old sentence
* this is the same on Invoiced and on Paid work orders, so the word "Invoiced" or "Paid" that tells the user why never appears on its own

The blocking itself works: the items are greyed out, the drop is refused and the lead does not change. Only the words are out of date.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Sign in to staging as an Admin and check the top bar shows **Staging Heavy Duty - 9919**.
2. Open a customer's **Approved** work order with a lead technician and finish it until its status is **Invoiced** (**Finance** tab > **Create Invoice**). Make a second one and take it on to **Paid**.
3. Open **Work Orders**, click the **All** tab, click **Board View**, and type the customer's name in **Search**.
4. Rest the pointer on the small lock icon next to the Invoiced card's number.

    * Its hover text reads `The lead technician can't be changed once a work order is Invoiced or Paid.`
    
5. Hover the Invoiced card, click its **More actions** (three dots), then rest the pointer on **Reassign lead technician**.

    * A tooltip shows `The lead technician can't be changed once a work order is Invoiced or Paid.`
    
6. Rest the pointer on **Unassign**.

    * The same sentence shows.
    
7. Press Escape. Drag the Invoiced card over another technician's column and, without letting go, read the note at the top of that column.

    * The note reads `The lead technician can't be changed once a work order is Invoiced or Paid.`
    
8. Let go. The card goes back to its technician (correct).
9. Repeat steps 4 to 9 with the Paid card, then in **Tech View** on the rows, dragging over another technician's group.

    * Every place shows the same old sentence.
    

**Actual Result:**

* The lock icon's hover text, every menu tooltip and every drag note on a locked work order read `The lead technician can't be changed once a work order is Invoiced or Paid.`

**Expected Result:**

* The PRD says: **"their tooltip reads “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” or “Paid · can’t be reassigned”, as in the design. The same words are the tooltip on the card’s or row’s lock icon, and the note shown at the top of another technician’s column or group while the work order is dragged over it"**

Change the List view button to the same columns icon, at the same size, so all three views match.

summary: Board and Tech View: open-hand pointer fingers show almost black instead of white
description:
Found while testing [SV-11588](https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-11588)

### Summary

In Board View and Tech View, the new open-hand pointer (the one you see while hovering over something you can drag) has almost all-black fingers. The top half of the hand looks black instead of white. The closed hand you see while dragging is fine.

### Steps to reproduce

Open the QA branch to reproduce the issue: [https://sv11588.qa.shopview.com/workorders](https://sv11588.qa.shopview.com/workorders)

1. Sign in as Admin.
2. Above the work order list, on the right, there are three small view icons. Click the middle one (`Tech View`).
3. Move the mouse pointer (don't click) over the column of six small grey dots at the very left of any row, just before the status label.
4. Look at the fingers of the hand pointer that appears. They are almost all black, not white with a black outline:

    ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=2481930e-2bb5-4907-854a-5532d6c61b16&&collection=&height=431&occurrenceKey=null&width=560&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null)
5. Now press and hold on those dots and drag a little. The closed hand that appears is white with a black outline. That is what the open hand should look like too.

**Fastest way to see it:** open [https://sv11588.qa.shopview.com/workorders](https://sv11588.qa.shopview.com/workorders), click the middle view icon (`Tech View`) and point at the six dots at the start of any row.

### Expected behaviour

The open hand is a white hand with a black outline, like the closed hand.

**Where this comes from:** [SV-11588](https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-11588), the ticket that introduced the new pointers: _"a white hand with a 2px black outline, the same shapes (open hand while hovering, closed hand while dragging), about 32px."_

### Current behaviour

At the size the pointer is actually shown, each finger of the open hand has at most one column of white pixels inside it, and the two middle fingers have none, only grey. So the fingers read as black. The same open hand shows everywhere it is used: Board View column headers, Tech View row dots and Tech View technician headers.

| **Pointer** | **What it looks like** |
| --- | --- |
| Open hand (hovering) | Fingers almost all black |
| Closed hand (dragging) | White with a black outline, as expected |

Tested on the QA branch sv11588, build v26.43.0-003b8fb, 22 October 2026.

summary: Board View and Tech View – View-Only User Never Sees "You Don't Have Permission to Assign Technicians"
description:
## Description

**When a user who may only view work orders tries to drag a card or row to another technician, the note "You don't have permission to assign technicians" should show at the top of that technician's column or group.** On staging nothing shows, so the user gets no explanation.

For example,

* the user presses on a card and moves the mouse to another technician's column: the card is not picked up, the mouse only highlights the card's text, and no note appears
* the same in Tech View on a row moved over another technician's group
* nothing is changed, which is correct — only the explanation is missing

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Sign in to staging as an Admin and check the top bar shows **Staging Heavy Duty - 9919**.
2. Go to your initials > **Settings** > **Roles & Permissions** and make a role whose **Work orders** permission has only **View** ticked. Give it to a staff member at this location (Settings > Staff).
3. Make two **Approved** work orders for one customer, both with the same lead technician, and make sure a second technician is active at this location.
4. Sign in as the view-only user. Open **Work Orders**, click the **All** tab, click **Board View**, and type the customer's name in **Search**.
5. Press on one of the cards and, keeping the mouse button down, move it over the second technician's column.

    * The card does not move with the mouse; its text gets highlighted.
    * No note appears at the top of the second technician's column.
    
6. Let go.

    * The card stays where it was (correct).
    
7. Click **Tech View** and do the same with the row, over the second technician's group.

    * Again no note appears.
    

**Actual Result:**

* No note shows anywhere. The card or row is simply not picked up, and the user is not told why.

**Expected Result:**

* The PRD says: **"A user without it who drags a card or row over another technician’s column or group sees the design’s note “You don’t have permission to assign technicians” at the top of that column or group, and the drop is refused."**

## Screenshots

summary: Board View and Tech View – Escape Does Not Close the Technician List After Clicking Into Its Search Box
description:
## Description

**Escape must close an open menu without changing anything — including the Technician filter's list when the cursor is in its "Search technician" box.** On staging, once you click into that box, Escape does nothing: the list stays open, even after pressing Escape again.

For example,

* the Technician list is opened and closed with Escape — it closes, as expected
* the list is opened again and the user clicks into **Search technician** (or types a name) — Escape no longer closes it; only a click outside does

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Sign in to staging as an Admin at **Staging Heavy Duty - 9919**.
2. Open **Work Orders**, click the **All** tab and click **Board View**.
3. Click the **Technician** filter, then press Escape.

    * The list closes.
    
4. Click the **Technician** filter again and click inside the **Search technician** box at the top of the list.
5. Press Escape, then press Escape again.

    * The list is still open both times.
    
6. Type a technician's first name (for example **Ralph**) in **Search technician** and press Escape.

    * The list is still open and the typed name stays.
    
7. Click **Tech View** in the display switcher and repeat steps 3 to 6.

    * The same happens in Tech View.
    

**Actual Result:**

* With the cursor in **Search technician**, Escape does not close the Technician list, in Board View and in Tech View.

**Expected Result:**

* Escape closes the Technician list without changing anything, wherever the cursor is in it. The PRD says: **"Escape closes an open menu, dialog or tooltip without changing anything."**

summary: Board View and Tech View – Keyboard Focus Is Lost When the Last Filtered Work Order Is Reassigned
description:
## Description

**When a keyboard user's move leaves nothing matching the filters, keyboard focus must move to the Clear all filters button of the "No work orders match these filters" message.** On staging the focus is lost: it falls to the page, so the next key does nothing.

For example,

* the Technician filter is set to one technician and that technician's last work order is reassigned with the keyboard
* the board is replaced by "No work orders match these filters", but no control has focus and the arrow keys do nothing

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Sign in to staging as an Admin at **Staging Heavy Duty - 9919**.
2. Make a customer with two **Approved** work orders led by one technician (for example **ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha**), and a second technician to move them to.
3. Open **Work Orders**, click the **All** tab and click **Board View**. Type the customer's name in **Search**.
4. Click **Technician** and tick the first technician. Press Escape.
5. Click in **Search**, then press **Tab** until the first card shows a focus ring.
6. Press **Tab** to reach the card's **More actions** (…) button, press **Enter**, choose **Reassign lead technician** with the arrow keys and press **Enter**. Pick the second technician and confirm.

    * The card leaves the column and the focus ring moves to the remaining card.
    
7. Do the same for the remaining card.

    * "No work orders match these filters" shows, but no focus ring is anywhere: the arrow keys do nothing and the next Tab jumps back to the top of the page.
    

**Actual Result:**

* Keyboard focus is lost to the page after the last work order leaves the result.

**Expected Result:**

* Focus moves to the **Clear all filters** button of "No work orders match these filters". The PRD says: **"When the focused work order leaves the result (for example after a filter change or a reassignment), focus moves to the next row or card in the same group or column, or to that group or column header when none is left. When the move leaves nothing matching the filters, so the board or table is replaced by the “No work orders match these filters” empty state (S1-N1a), for example moving the last work order of the only technician chosen in the Technician filter, focus moves to its Clear all filters button."**

summary: Board View – The Whole Page Scrolls, Although the PRD Lets Only the Columns Scroll
description:
## Description

**What the PRD requires:** in Board View the page itself must never scroll up or down — only the cards inside each column may scroll (PRD **S3-E1**: "The page itself does not scroll vertically; only the content inside each column does.").

**What happens instead:** on production the page itself has become scrollable. Turning the mouse wheel over an empty part of the board moves the whole page, and the toolbar (tabs, **Search**, filters, view switcher) slides off the top of the screen.

**Why the page can scroll now:**

* at a 1600 px wide window the row of tabs, **Search** and filters no longer fits since the **Technician** filter was added (<custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-0">https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-11326#icft=SV-11326</custom>, Done 20 Oct 2026), so **Create Work Order** drops to a second line
* that pushes the board 56 px lower, so the page (1056 px) is taller than the window (1000 px) and has room to move
* the wheel over an empty area under a short column scrolls that extra space, taking the tabs, **Search**, the filters and the view switcher out of sight
* scrolling inside a column with many cards works correctly — only that column moves

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Sign in to production and check the top bar shows **Truck Hill 1**; use a browser window about 1600 × 1000.
2. Open **Work Orders**, click the **All** tab, type `ZZAUTOTEST F2 Column Scroll` in **Search** and click **Board View**.

    * **Unassigned** holds many cards; the technician columns next to it are short or empty.
    * **Create Work Order** sits on its own line under the row of tabs and filters.
    
3. Put the mouse over the empty area below a short column (e.g. under **Ayesha Khan**) and turn the wheel down.

    * The whole page moves up: the **All / Estimates / Work Orders / Completed** tabs, **Search**, the filters and the view switcher go off the top.
    

**Actual Result:**

* The page itself scrolls: one turn of the wheel moves the whole page by 56 px and the toolbar goes out of sight.

**Expected Result:**

* As the PRD requires (S3-E1), the page itself does not scroll; only the content inside each column scrolls.

## Screenshots

summary: Board Card – More Actions Button Sits Beside the Status Label, Not Over It
description:
## Description

**What the design requires:** when the mouse is over a Board View card, the **…** (More actions) button appears at the card's top right, **over the right end of the status label**, covering part of it. The design names this state "board card menu button over badge". The PRD only says the button appears on hover or keyboard focus (**S3-R13**) and says nothing about where it sits, so the design is the source for its position.

**What happens instead:** the **…** button appears **beside** the status label, to its left, and the status label is shown in full.

For example:

* on an Approved work order the design shows **Appro…** with the **…** button on top of the rest of the word
* the build shows the full word **Approved** with the **…** button in a space to its left

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Sign in and open **Work Orders**, click the **All** tab and click **Board View** in the display switcher.
2. Find the card of any work order with a status label (e.g. **Approved**).
3. Move the mouse over the card.

    * The card's border darkens and the **…** button appears at the top right.
    * The **…** button sits to the left of the status label; the label is not covered.
    

**Actual Result:**

* The **…** button sits beside the status label, to its left.

**Expected Result:**

summary: Board View and Tech View: hand cursor turns invisible white on Windows; use our own outlined hand
description:
### What

In Board View and Tech View, the hand cursor you see over cards, rows and technician headers (and while dragging) can turn pure white with no outline, so it disappears against the white cards. The normal arrow is fine.

The cause: these views use the browser's own grab and grabbing hands. Chrome on Windows draws those itself, ignoring the user's Windows pointer settings, and on some screens they come out white with no outline.

### Fix

* Replace the browser's grab and grabbing hands in Board View and Tech View with our own hand cursors: a white hand with a 2px black outline, the same shapes (open hand while hovering, closed hand while dragging), about 32px.
* Keep the browser's grab / grabbing as the fallback, so a browser that cannot show a custom cursor still shows a hand.
* Apply it everywhere these views use a hand today: Board View cards and column headers, Tech View rows and group headers, and while dragging in either view.
* Nothing else changes: same places, same moments, only the drawing of the hand.

### How to check

* On Windows in Chrome, hover a Board View card, a Tech View row and a technician header: the hand has a clear black outline on white and on blue.
* Drag a card or row: the closed hand keeps its black outline the whole drag.
* List and every other page are unchanged.

### Reproduced

Windows 11, Chrome, standard Windows pointer, one 1920x1080 screen: the browser's grab and grabbing hands went pure white, while a hand drawn with a black outline stayed visible. Chris Ward, 2026-10-20.

---

**Test case for this issue:** [C707078](https://shopview.testrail.io/index.php?/cases/view/707078) On Windows Chrome the hand pointer has a black outline in Board and Tech View

**Test run:** not in the WO Board and Tech View test run (run 498) yet: the case is in the Fast-follow folder, because this ticket is a fast follow.
